passage:
Mentor's note, week five. In group project meetings I have seen Indu correct Payal's English in front of everyone and roll her eyes when Payal spoke about her school in a small town. Payal has gone quiet and now sends her slides by message instead of presenting.

I asked Indu to stay after class. She was defensive at first: "I'm only being honest." When I asked what she was afraid of, she was silent, then said her first-semester marks were poor and everyone else seemed to speak better than her. It felt good, she admitted, to have someone she could look down on.

I did not scold her. I suggested she read Payal's slides properly before the next meeting. This week Indu asked Payal about her data, and I saw Payal present again. I will keep watching.

qa.q: What did Payal start doing instead of presenting?
What did Indu's answer show about her feelings behind the eye-rolling?
qa.a: Insecurity. Indu feared being behind and said it felt good to have someone to look down on.

qa.q: How did the mentor help without lecturing?
qa.a: They asked what Indu was afraid of, did not scold, and suggested reading Payal's slides properly.

qa.q: How might Payal have felt in the meetings before this?
qa.a: Embarrassed and small. Going quiet suggests Payal was avoiding more corrections in front of everyone.

grounding: Indu looks down on Payal for background and English; the contempt is traced to insecurity and Indu begins to treat Payal as an equal.

passage:
In the shared kitchen of their student residence in Madrid, Lucia rolled her eyes when Olga asked, in slow, careful Spanish, whether the oven was "hot of before". Lucia's friends laughed. Later Lucia repeated it in the group chat.
That evening in her English seminar, the professor asked Lucia to read aloud. Her face burned at every word she stumbled over, and she hated the silence while the others waited. Walking home, it hit her: the kitchen laugh had felt good because, for once, someone else was the one fumbling.
Next morning Olga was in the kitchen again, frowning at the dishwasher instructions. Lucia sat down beside her. "Preheated, you mean. We say 'precalentado'. It's a silly word." Olga smiled, surprised. "In Ukrainian we also have silly words." They made coffee and swapped silly words for twenty minutes. Lucia deleted her message from the group chat before class.

qa.q: What did Olga ask in the kitchen?
qa.a: Whether the oven was "hot of before".

qa.q: What did Lucia realise on the walk home after her seminar?
qa.a: That mocking Olga felt good because, for once, someone else was fumbling; the contempt hid her own embarrassment and insecurity.

qa.q: What did Lucia do next morning to treat Olga as an equal?
qa.a: She sat beside Olga, kindly gave her the word "precalentado", swapped words over coffee, and deleted the mocking message.

qa.q: How might Olga have experienced the kitchen laughter?
qa.a: As lonely and humiliating, being laughed at while trying hard in a new language.

grounding: Shows looking down on someone for their language, seeing that the contempt hides one's own insecurity, and treating them as an equal.

passage:
At the IT company's training centre in Mysuru, the eight trainees were split into teams for the final demo. Chetan, the team lead, kept the presentation, gave the slides to two friends, and handed Gopika the testing. "Your English, no? Clients won't get it." He said it lightly. The others smiled.
Gopika said nothing and ran tests till nine every night.
On demo day, the client's engineer asked a hard question about a failing case. Chetan froze. Gopika stood up and explained it slowly, simply, precise down to the line number. The engineer nodded.
That night Chetan couldn't sleep. Since joining, he had been scared that his own college wasn't good enough; mocking Gopika's English had made him feel less small. It hadn't made him better.
Next morning he went to her desk. "I was wrong about you, and about why I said it. Will you present the testing section next week?" Gopika considered him for a long moment. "Yes. And you'll check your own slides for once."

qa.q: Which task did Chetan hand Gopika?
What feeling was really behind Chetan's remark about Gopika's English?
qa.a: His own fear that his college wasn't good enough; mocking her made him feel less small, a hidden insecurity.

qa.q: What did Chetan do to put things right?
qa.a: He admitted he was wrong about Gopika and about his reason, and asked her to present the testing section next week.

qa.q: How might Gopika have felt during the weeks before the demo?
qa.a: Belittled and left out, yet determined, working on the tests till nine every night.

grounding: Illustrates contempt for a colleague's English that hides insecurity, and the shift to treating her as an equal.
